rendered: The sodiation of the carbon layer provides only a small capacity, 0.05 mAh/cm^2[1] (or 120 mAh/g[2]). The paper calls this negligible compared with the plating capacities, which go up to 12 mAh/cm^2[3]. In the plating tests shown in Fig. 2[4], loadings run from 0.5 mAh/cm^2[5] (at 1[6] mA/cm^2 for a 30[7] min plating time) up to 8 mAh/cm^2[8], and 50[9] cycles were run at 12 mAh/cm^2[10]. So the sodiation step contributes only a small fraction of the plated capacity at the lowest loading shown, and far less at the highest. The meaningful capacity comes from the in situ plating of sodium metal, not from the carbon layer.
